chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Saeed al-Qammat, from al-Mufazzal, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, teach me a comprehensive supplication.' So he said to me, 'Praise Allah, for there would not remain anyone who prays except that he supplicates for you, saying, 'Allah hears the one who praises Him'.'

key_terms.سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ: Allah hears the one who praises Him (a phrase from Surah Al-Baqarah recited in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the most comprehensive supplication according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the profound efficacy of 'Alhamdulillah' as a universal supplication, noting that since every worshipper recites it during their obligatory prayers, the one who initiates it is continuously included in the intercessory prayers of the entire community. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on the communal nature of worship and the spiritual benefit of being remembered by others in their direct communion with Allah. The narration reflects the scholarly view that simple, frequent acts of remembrance carry immense weight due to their ubiquity in the daily ritual of the Ummah.
